name: Fall Silent
label: Revelation
lede: Fall Silent started in Reno with Crowbar records and punk 7"s, got Levi Watson beaten up in Salt Lake City over one song, and found its biggest audience in Japan because Max Ward wore their shirt. Watson crashed the car in New Jersey in 2002, the band ended a year later, and it came back in 2015 with Watson now a math teacher.

eras.title: Crowbar fans in the high desert
eras.text: Brothers Levi Watson and Damon Watson came out of New Blood; Danny Galecki and Brian Wohlgemuth came out of Sister Mary 12". In Reno they wanted Crowbar, '90s death metal and '80s punk in the same song, and the first 7" wouldn't even play at the right speed.

years.h: Four Reno kids start Fall Silent
years.p: Levi Watson sings, his brother Damon Watson drums, Danny Galecki plays guitar and names the band, and Brian Wohlgemuth plays bass.

years.h: The first 7" is pressed at 500 copies and plays wrong
years.p: Never Forget... comes out on the band's own label with technical trouble around its 45 rpm format. A split 7" with Wellington follows on Fetus Records, run through Ryan Butler, later of Unruh.

years.h: No Strength to Suffer, self-released under the RPT name
years.p: Seventeen songs recorded at Sierra Sonics, on the band's Revolutionary Power Tools label. Revelation later called Fall Silent possibly the angriest band around.
years.xp:
The album brought odd timing, more dynamics and more technical guitar parts, with Crowbar and Meshuggah in the mix.

Revelation's catalog lists it as 1996. Watson's own interview with No Echo puts it in 1997.

q: It was the most fun we had on any tour we ever did.
years.h: Twenty shows with Gehenna, a CBGB matinee and Spazz in San Francisco
years.p: The "Eat, Fight, Fuck" tour of 1996 ran about a month behind No Strength to Suffer, with Epicenter in San Francisco alongside [[Spazz|30185d89-e9b1-4083-8a58-4688e10e0ec8]].
years.xp: It was the band's first time on the road for real. "We were finally living like real rock bands. Traveling around, meeting people, and constantly talking shit," Watson told No Echo.

years.big: "I got beat up really bad in Salt Lake City for playing that song."
years.h: One song gets Levi Watson beaten up in Salt Lake City
years.p: Watson wrote Looking In against Reno's violent hardline kids; plenty heard it as anti-straight edge. Watson is the one who got hurt.
years.xp:
Watson says members of Unconquered and their friends took $1,800 of Fall Silent's merch money, broke their car windows and slashed their tires.

He still insists it's an anti-hardline song, not an anti-straight edge one. Fall Silent still play it.

eras.title: Big in Japan
eras.text: At home Fall Silent stayed a Reno secret. In Japan they had fans from the first 7" on, and Levi Watson credits one photo of Spazz's Max Ward in a Fall Silent shirt.

years.p: Fall Silent's second album, on Revolutionary Power Tools. Japan gets its own edition with full lyric translations, and 702 and Slovenly press it on vinyl in 1999.

years.h: Max Ward releases Life: Beautiful, But Heartless
years.p: The 7" comes out on the [[Spazz|30185d89-e9b1-4083-8a58-4688e10e0ec8]] drummer's label and spreads fast in Japan. It's bassist Roger Colestock's last recording with the band.

years.big: "I think that photo, on that record, is about 80% of why people in Japan like us so much."
years.p: Fall Silent's first overseas tour. Watson means Max Ward in a Fall Silent shirt on the cover of Spazz's Sweatin' II: Deported Live Gorilla.
years.xp: Japanese crowds, Watson says, had better venues and better merch tables, and they bought CDs. Every Fall Silent release has sold well there since.

eras.title: Revelation, then a wreck in New Jersey
eras.text: Revelation collected the out-of-print records and put out a new album with two younger death metal fans in the band. The tour behind it ended in a wreck, and the band came apart within a year.

years.h: Revelation collects three records on Six Years in the Desert
years.p: A remastered CD of No Strength to Suffer, Nineteenhundredninetyseven and the Life: Beautiful, But Heartless 7". Levi Watson's son is born the same year.
Two death metal fans, guitarist Donny Johnson and bassist Justin Spalin, join and push Fall Silent straighter and heavier, with fewer odd time signatures.

years.h: Watson crashes the car in New Jersey and the tour ends
years.p: The Revelation-booked Drunken Violence tour went through the South to Florida, then up the East Coast. Watson dates the beginning of the end to that wreck.

years.h: Fall Silent break up in summer 2003
years.p: Watson lists a new son, a marriage ending, the failed tour, a band drifting apart and Damon Watson's struggles with substances. He didn't want to do Fall Silent again.

eras.title: Mr. Watson, math teacher
eras.text: Levi Watson went back to school and taught math for twelve years, winning awards for it. Damon Watson moved home from Seattle and started Old Glory with Danny Galecki, and the two of them talked Levi back.

years.h: The day after Christmas, Fall Silent play a Reno bar
years.p: No advance promotion. Levi Watson, Damon Watson and Danny Galecki play as Fall Silent for the first time in twelve years.
Revelation REV 168, mastered by Ryan Butler at Arcane Digital. Watson picks Try Harder as the song that sums up the band: grind, thrash and punk in one.
years.xp: Revelation pressed 330 on gold and 770 on red/black marble. Joe Foley joined on guitar, with a two-guitar line-up planned.

years.h: Seventeen years on, Japan again, with Watson's 15-year-old on merch
years.p: Watson brings his son Jude to sell shirts. A Japanese band called Superstructure puts Fall Silent's album art on its merch and hosts an annual No Strength to Suffer festival.
years.xp: It was July 2017, 17 years after the first Japan tour. Watson told No Echo every Fall Silent release still sells well there.

eras.title: You Knew I Was Poison
eras.text: The first Fall Silent album in nearly two decades came out in the middle of the pandemic, with Joe Foley now on bass. The old records still weren't on vinyl, and one fan tried to change that.

years.h: You Knew I Was Poison lands on Revelation
years.p: Eight songs from Levi Watson, Damon Watson, Danny Galecki and Joe Foley. Two Plus Two Is Five takes on reading the Bible literally.
years.xp: Revelation pressed 300 on red, plus a RevHQ-only white/black splatter of 100 that sold out. Watson, by then a middle school math teacher, said his wife's piercing studio had been shut ten weeks by the pandemic.

years.h: A Change.org petition asks Revelation for the old records on vinyl
years.p: A fan wants Six Years in the Desert and Drunken Violence pressed, both CD-only since the early 2000s. It closes with 27 supporters.
